title: Interactive AI assistance for predictive and flexible control in discharge and transition management: Development phase (KIAFlex-Research)
summary:
Every day, hospitals discharge patients who require continued care in medical/nursing or rehabilitative facilities after their hospital stay. This further treatment by other care providers is organized by discharge management (DM). Currently, organization and communication with follow-up care providers is done via paper, fax, and telephone. This leads to a great deal of work for DM employees and sometimes, a loss of information, as transparency is not always guaranteed.  

The project presented here (KIAFlex-Research) is the second phase of the KIAFlex project and focuses on the development of an AI model that can accurately predict the length of stay and potential need for follow-up care. The prediction model will be trained with previous patient data and clinical decisions.
conditions: No specific diseases are examined. The project aims to develop an AI-based assistance system to optimize clinical and administrative processes in discharge management. The prediction models for the system will be trained on clinical cases in order to realistically predict follow-up care needs and discharge dates.

interventions.name: The AI model to be developed here will be trained using retrospektive inpatient cases in the DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group) fee schedule (somatic medicine) from both the University Hospital Mannheim and the University Hospital Bonn. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are all inpatient treatment cases in the german diagnosis-related groups (ger. DRG) fee area (somatic medicine) in the period covered (inpatient cases with discharge from 01.01.2019 - 31.12.2023).
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are all inpatient treatment cases in the compensation system for psychiatric and psychosomatic institutions (ger. PEPP) fee area (psychiatry, psychosomatics, geriatric psychiatry), as different framework conditions apply to social services staff in these areas.
